text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly where the pain is in your right groin and how your leg is positioned right now?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. I need to assess the integrity of the hip joint, so please remain still while I gently palpate the area and attempt to passively rotate the affected leg. Does this movement cause a sharp increase in pain, and are you able to bear any weight on that right leg?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text: The position of your leg—shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated—is a classic sign of a posterior hip dislocation. To confirm this and rule out associated fractures, I will order an immediate X-ray. REQUEST TEST: Pelvis_X-Ray
